result.title: EvoViM: Recursively Self-Evolving Visual Agents for Exploration with Deferred Queries
result.summary: Multimodal large language model (MLLM) agents have shown promising capabilities in task-oriented environments. However, they still struggle when queries are deferred until after exploration, requiring them to retain visual evidence before knowing which details will matter. We introduce EvoViM, a recursively self-evolving framework in which a frozen multimodal model turns its own interaction experience into one visual program for memory and skills. The program retains images and computes directly on pixels, and its operations decide how this evidence is used in each task. During memory evolution, the same model traces failures in its visual trajectories to the operations that lost or misused evidence and revises them. It also rewrites the notes and analysis tools that guide later revisions, which then build on earlier findings and skip changes that have already failed. We evaluate EvoViM with three multimodal models on six tasks covering visual matching, spatial recall, and sequential decision-making, including three tasks with deferred queries. Across the six tasks, EvoViM improves the average score over AutoMem, the strongest baseline in the main comparison, by 31.3-47.6 points on held-out episodes. Programs written once from the initial environment instructions perform substantially worse, highlighting the value of interaction experience in shaping how visual evidence is retained and used. Code and dataset are available at https://evovim.github.io/.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EvoViM：冻结多模态模型将交互经验写成可递归修订的视觉程序，直接保留图像并在像素上计算，同时回溯失败到丢失或误用证据的操作；在六个含延迟查询的任务上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作正面处理延迟查询下视觉证据的保留、筛选与使用，并做证据丢失/误用的操作级归因，与 LVR 的视觉细节保留和贡献分配直接相关；不过其状态存于外部视觉程序而非模型 latent，可供对照核查。
